newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST-Unigate H1 profit seen static.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Unigate H1 profit seen static.

text.p: British food and distribution group Unigate Plc is expected to report little changed first-half pretax profits on Tuesday.
Analysts are looking for pretax profits of anywhere between 57 to 59 million stg for the half year to September 30, compared with 60.4 million previously.
Unigate, like fellow milk producers, will have felt the pinch from weakness in dairy commodity prices, analysts said .
The company said in July that current trading was broadly in line with expectations, but it warned that weak dairy commodity prices were not reflected in lower milk costs.
However, analysts said they will be more interested in seeing the effect that a busy year on the acquisition and disposal front has had on the company.

"Unigate has had an awful lot of acquisitions and disposals and in the comparitive figures there was a contribution from Nutricia and the U.S restaurant business," said Michael Bourke, an analyst at Panmure Gordon.

Panmure estimates that Unigate will make pre-tax profits of 59 million stg and forecasts that the dividend will be increased to 7p from 6.65p previously. Earnings per share are seen coming in at 18.4p compared with 18.8.
"The main issue at Unigate is not the result but how they are going to spend their cash and what is the potential borrowing ability," said one analyst at a British bank.
He saw Unigate beefing up the chilled food and distribution sides of the group.
Analysts also said they would be keen to see how Unigate's purchase of Kraft Food International's Vitalite and Golden Churn brands in the UK and its Valle brand in Italy had fared so far.
Unigate paid 77.25 million stg in cash to U.S. food and tobacco giant Philip Morris for the businesses.
